body: Thanks for the report @rheineke - if you want to take a look at fixing it do let us know :D

@birdsarah I think the right way to fix this issue is somewhere on the Javascript side. The datepicker input is '08/01/2016' so I assume Javascript is converting this to a datetime object and then serializing it again to 'Mon Aug 01 2016 00:00:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time)'. The serialization is probably using a system default datetime format. For me, the challenge is that I have very little idea how BokehJS works aside glossing over the [dev guide](http://bokeh.pydata.org/en/latest/docs/dev_guide/setup.html#devguide-setup).

Pretty sure the `d.toString()` call on line 26 of https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh/blob/master/bokehjs/src/coffee/models/widgets/date_picker.coffee just needs to be given an explicit date format string like `d.toString('yyyy-mm-dd')`

I have a relatively simple fix that has worked for me since I put this ticket in. I'll commit and make a pull request this weekend.

For anyone who wants to fix it now in bokeh 0.12.4, change line 1052 of bokeh/core/properties.py to
`value = dateutil.parser.parse(value.split(' (')[0]).date()`

Essentially, the problem is that Windows (Chrome) has a different default datetime format that includes the timezone in parentheses. The code change above intercepts this at deserialization in Python. A more elegant solution would be to specify the datetime format at serialization in JS.

@bryevdv I can confirm the findings of @artur-scholz. 
The problem is in date_picker.coffee.
```
  _on_select: (date) =>
    @model.value = date.toString()
    @change_input()
```
Resulting on win10/IE to: "'Sun Sep 24 2017 00:00:00 GMT+0200 (Mitteleuropäische Sommerzeit)'
Fix is easy. 
```
  _on_select: (date) =>
    @model.value = date.toISOString()
    @change_input()
```
Resulting to: "2017-09-22T22:00:00.00Z"

The former cannot be parsed by dateutil:
```
>>> value = dateutil.parser.parse('Sun Sep 24 2017 00:00:00 GMT+0200 (Mitteleuropäische Sommerzeit)')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/volker/workspace/eprofile/lib/python3.5/site-packages/python_dateutil-2.6.1-py3.5.egg/dateutil/parser.py", line 559, in parse
    raise ValueError("Unknown string format")
ValueError: Unknown string format
```
The later can be parsed.
```
>>> dateutil.parser.parse('2017-09-22T22:00:00.00Z')
datetime.datetime(2017, 9, 22, 22, 0, tzinfo=tzutc())
```
@bryevdv  Shall I create a PR?
@volkerjaenisch yes please, and thanks for running this down
